core_obligations: Derive the local criterion (2) from localisation of the dualizing complex and the algebraic Cohen-Macaulay criterion (proof lines 6230-6236).
Prove openness and Cohen-Macaulayness of the locus U by shrinking an affine neighbourhood so that only the cohomology in degree n_x survives (proof lines 6238-6250).
Deduce (1) in both directions and, in the connected Cohen-Macaulay case, that the dualizing complex is a shift of a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module (proof lines 6252-6268).
proof_roadmap: Openness of the Cohen-Macaulay locus (proof lines 6238-6250).
difficulty_reason: For a locally Noetherian scheme X with dualizing complex omega, the lemma asserts three equivalences and statements: X is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if omega locally has a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf, the local ring O_{X,x} is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the localised complex has a unique nonzero cohomology, and the Cohen-Macaulay locus is open and Cohen-Macaulay; moreover if X is connected and Cohen-Macaulay then omega = omega_X[-n] for a coherent Cohen-Macaulay module omega_X and some integer n (statement lines 6213-6228). The proof first notes that by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-dualizing-localize the localised complex is a dualizing complex over O_{X,x}, so Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-apply-CM gives (2) (proof lines 6230-6236). For (3), if O_{X,x} is Cohen-Macaulay with unique nonvanishing cohomology in degree n_x, then locally omega lies in D^b_Coh so only finitely many cohomology sheaves are nonzero, and after shrinking to an affine neighbourhood only H^{n_x} survives by Modules, Lemma labelled modules-lemma-finite-type-stalk-zero, which shows simultaneously that U is open and Cohen-Macaulay (proof lines 6238-6250). Statement (1) then follows: the backward implication from (2), and the forward one from the previous paragraph (proof lines 6252-6258). Finally, if X is connected and Cohen-Macaulay the map x -> n_x is locally constant hence constant, and omega_X = H^n(omega) is Cohen-Macaulay by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-apply-CM and the definition of a Cohen-Macaulay module (proof lines 6260-6268). Turning the local uniqueness of the nonvanishing cohomology into openness by shrinking an affine neighbourhood is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
